newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - April 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - April 8.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Tuesday's Daily Variety:
* Creative Artists Agency talent agent and agency co-chairman Jack Rapke has resigned to pursue other possibilities in entertainment.
* General Electric's NBC has renewed Late Night host Conan O'Brien for five more years, expanding a one-year deal.

* Westinghouse CEO Michael Jordan on Monday said that the rising cost of broadcasting in the information era is outstripping revenue growth, forcing industry consolidation and creating a need for reforms in advertiser media buying.
* Columbia Pictures has picked up the project "All the Pretty Horses," based on the best-selling novel, for Mike Nichols to produce but not direct, the studio said.
* Scott Hicks, who directed the critically acclaimed "Shine", has committed to his next film -- Universal Pictures' drama "Snow Falling on Cedars."

* News Corp 20th Century Fox has signed Chris Columbus and his 1492 Pictures to write, produce and direct films. Columbus' relationship with Fox resulted in the comedy hits "Home Alone," "Home Alone 2" and "Mrs Doubtfire."

* With studios now concentrating nearly all of their marketing and distribution power on the initial days of a theatrical release, a solid weekend is no longer a guarantee of long-range box office success.
